_comment: Turkish terms chosen for the functionalism-interactionism lesson. status: ok = attested in a Turkish source I opened (TÜBİTAK Ansiklopedi entries, see bibliography); chosen = my own rendering of an English term (no Turkish source checked); check = seen only in search-engine results or weakly attested, needs a Turkish-language reviewer. See content/research-notes/functionalism-interactionism.md.

structural-functionalism.note: TÜBİTAK Ansiklopedi has the entry ‘Yapısal işlevselcilik’ and a separate ‘İşlevselcilik (Sosyoloji)’. ‘Yapısal-fonksiyonel’ is seen only in the title of a Turkish web page in search results (not opened): check.

dysfunction.note: TÜBİTAK’s ‘Yapısal işlevselcilik’ uses ‘işlevsizlik’ in the sense of Merton’s dysfunctions; a Turkish article on Merton in a DergiPark journal was seen (abstract only, through a summary) using a different wording (‘bozuk işlev’). Not used.

manifest-function.note: TÜBİTAK Ansiklopedi (‘Yapısal işlevselcilik’: ‘açık işlevler’; ‘İşlevselcilik (Sosyoloji)’: ‘gizil ve açık işlev’).

latent-function.note: ‘Gizil’ in TÜBİTAK ‘İşlevselcilik (Sosyoloji)’; ‘gizli işlevler’ in TÜBİTAK ‘Yapısal işlevselcilik’. The lesson uses ‘gizil’ and mentions ‘gizli’.

functional-alternative.note: Merton’s ‘functional alternatives / equivalents / substitutes’; no Turkish source checked.

functional-prerequisite.note: A Turkish search summary mentioned ‘işlevsel ön gereklilik’; not verified, not used.

latency-pattern-maintenance.note: ‘Gizil örüntü sürdürme’ in ‘İşlevselcilik (Sosyoloji)’; the other entry keeps ‘latent pattern maintenance’ in English.

symbolic-interactionism.note: Course unit title and TÜBİTAK Ansiklopedi entry (Ahmet Özalp). ‘Sembolik etkileşim (teorisi)’ seen only in web-page titles in search results: check.

looking-glass-self.note: Seen in Turkish web pages listed in search results (not opened); not in the TÜBİTAK entry summary.

generalized-other.note: Seen in Turkish web pages listed in search results (not opened).

i-and-me.note: Kept in English letters with an explanation in the lesson; no established Turkish pair verified.

play-game-stage.note: Turkish ‘oyun’ would translate both words; the lesson keeps the English terms in brackets.

thomas-theorem.note: Merton’s name for the sentence; the Turkish rendering is ours.

structure-agency.note: ‘Fail’ for ‘agency’ is a common Turkish social-theory rendering but was not verified in a source I opened.

grand-theory.note: The earlier lesson what-is-theory uses ‘büyük boy kuram’ for the different notion of ‘grand theory’ as a size class; here Mills’s polemical label is rendered ‘büyük kuram’.

narcotizing-dysfunction.note: The English term is kept in brackets; no Turkish source verified.
